items.text: Net $400 or more from side work? Self-employment tax applies (15.3%).

ig_caption:
Paid for side work this year and no 1099 showed up? The money is still taxable.

For 2026, fewer people will get a form at all:

✔️ 1099-NEC: a client only has to send one once they pay you $2,000 or more.
✔️ 1099-K: payment apps send one once you pass $20,000 and 200 sales.
✔️ The IRS is clear: form or no form, you report the income.
✔️ Net $400 or more from side work means self-employment tax (15.3%) on top of income tax.

The best time to plan for it is before Dec 31. In a year-end session we total your side income, check what you can still deduct and set your Jan 15 payment.

Comment PLAN and we'll send you the link, or find it at mfa-advisory.com/year-end-tax-planning

li_caption:
Many people with side income will get no 1099 for 2026. The income is still taxable.

Myth vs fact:

1. Myth: no 1099 means nothing to report. Fact: the IRS says you must report your income whether or not you receive a form.
2. Fact: fewer 1099-NECs are coming. For payments made in 2026, a business only has to send one once it pays you $2,000 or more.
3. Fact: fewer 1099-Ks too. Payment apps and online marketplaces only have to send one when payments pass $20,000 and 200 transactions.
4. Fact: net earnings of $400 or more from self-employment bring self-employment tax of 15.3% (Social Security and Medicare), on top of income tax.

So the bill can arrive in April with no paper trail to warn you. Your own records are what count: deposits, app reports and invoices.

December is the time to deal with it. In a year-end planning session we total your side income, look at what you can still deduct before Dec 31 and set the Jan 15, 2027 estimated payment if you need one.

Comment PLAN and we will send it.
